top4.why: Wednesday's flush to $157.25 turned out to be a bear trap: Thursday's +2.2% engulfing candle came on three mega-cap beats, and ABT and UNH raised guidance. This is quality defense with earnings behind it, and a weekly close above $164-165.61 opens new highs.

It has the strongest chart in the brief (+5.2% for the week, 50-day reclaimed Monday and held) and is the direct hedge on the war and oil shock driving the Fed officials' hawkish talk. Hold it with a stop at $56.52, because both lenses warn that geopolitical gaps can fade and Friday's volume was light.

The index fell 1.4%, but underneath it cash-flow cyclicals took the lead from the AI-capex names: UNP and CSX made new highs, UPS rose 4.7% and ITW 4.3%. That is the broad rotation (equal-weight beating cap-weight) inside one sector, and Thursday's earnings cluster is the catalyst to break out of the range between the 20-day and 50-day averages.

It printed a new 52-week high in a risk-off week on PLD's beat-and-raise, with O, WELL and SPG also delivering, so it is a landing spot for money leaving semis and a rates counterweight to Energy. The risks are that its 3.19% yield sits 133 bps below the 4.52% 10-year and that the data-center REITs trade like the Nasdaq.
